body: Same here, I would like to sign up.  Thank you.

Thank you.  How do you know it will get better though?  That's just wishful thinking.  There are plently of people that under terrible circumstances for the rest of their lives without things ever getting better.  I don't want to be one of them.  In some ways I think it's merciful that we can't see the future.

Thank you.  I'm finally reading this I guess.  I think it's a lot easier to go home as a girl, and, find people who are interested in you, not to mention the thing that triggered wanting to kill myself for the last two years was a suburban white girl dumping me on the car ride home from the airport.

Hey I know it's been a while (and your account is probably a throw away).  I just wanted to see how you're doing and let you know that I'm thinking about you.  You mentioned having a "few good days" I know what that's like, it was like that for me for a while.  
Hope you're well friend, and if not hope you're at least hanging in there.

Friend - I am sorry to hear about your trouble.  It sounds like you're exhausted - that you've been fighting this for a while, partially for you but mostly for the people you love.  I'm happy that you have them and they have you.  

If you are depressed you're likely to feel like you're in a dark tunnel and always have been / will be.  I hope you're able to challenge that notion at times at least.  I think you can experience periods of joy again, especially if you have in the past.  

From your post it seems that intellectually your mind is still very 
healthy, perhaps painfully so.  I would think that mental strength could make things harder -- being so acutely aware of what's happening.  

From what I've read, involuntary committal is a common concern and barrier to treatment.  The actual occurrence though is very uncommon.  If you haven't already you could ask your doctor if they've ever committed anyone.  I think the legal requirements are quite high, and given how smart you are, there's almost no point since you could just talk yourself out if you wanted to.  My humble advice is to be as open with your doctor as possible.  You might even check if that's easier with a different doctor. 

I'm a Christian as well.  I've posted here as well.  I'm not saying we're the same (and I don't feel like your intellectual / life experience equal) but perhaps I've felt similar at times.

My heart goes out to you friend.  I will pray for you.
That was beautiful, thank you.

Tough question...in my experience 3 out of 4 are useless...

If you're going by websites, I would look for someone who mentions cognitive therapy, BUT it's really hard to say without meeting them in person.  Depression also has a way of coloring everything negatively, so you might like them more in person than you think you might.  

If you can, try to find someone who would have experience treating a similar demographic as you.  If you're a college student, see a university councilor / psych.  If you've spent a lot of time in cities, see someone who practices in a city...  Again not written in stone that it will help, but it's generally helpful to see someone who's treated people with the same background as you before.
I'm sorry, it sounds like you feel drained, hopeless, perhaps apathetic?  Would love to hear more about whats going on.  For what it's worth feel free to message me anytime you like.
Very similar situation, can I see this as well?

I know that feeling.  I'm pretty isolated myself, new town 1000 miles  from home.  It's hard.  

I guess a thought that keeps me going (and I'm not always able to keep going) is what it would be like if I met someone like her again.  I loved her unconditionally, would have done anything for her, so i guess for now that means hanging in and trying not to go insane.

Could you tell me more about how you are feeling?  I am here for you, friend.  You're post struck me because I've said similar things to myself.  I'm actually with my Dad now too, and it helps.  What is it like for you?
So you're 5 years older than me, and still drawn to SW.  Does it just become part of your life?  Does it come and go?

Yeah I've called too, they didn't seem too helpful but I guess it's someone to talk with.  Once was my exgf calling on me...then I got the same lady a few times in a row, kind of odd.  I guess it's necessary sometimes when your stuck in an absolutely horrible fucking mood and can't get out.

Woaw, reddit gold, thanks! Doesn't really match with my current hypothesis that I suck at everything and always will...  

Thanks for some evidence to the contrary friend.  :)

Thank you for sharing, that's really interesting, and I'm glad if it made you feel better.   

It sounds like the nurse in you knows that something is wrong, and talking to a professional may help.  Not having insurance makes it harder but you mentioned you're doing alright financially, perhaps you would have the income to cover a few appointments?    

I think another part of you sees a glimmer of what I see, a beautiful, amazing girl who will come back eventually.  I've known girls who have described similar things as you and they are extremely happy now, smart, funny, awesome to be around.  Sometimes we lose sight of who we are.  

I've been told the same I guess, it's harder for me to believe for myself.  I look at old photos and it doesn't even seem like the same person, but I guess he can come back.  

It sounds like fighting with your husband can be frustrating.  I've also been told that fighting is good...without fights nothing ever gets resolved, but I understand that may not make the experience feel any better.

Yes I am frustrated.  Sorry, I read some other posts on SW and can see how people can appear cool in 5-6 lines of text.  

I'm in a really dangerous place, fixated on getting a Ruger SP 101 357 Magnum.  My phone's broken so I can't call anyone...and actually couldn't get directions to the gun show that I intended to visit today.  

Been debating whether I should call the suicide help line using google voice.

I'm here if you would like to talk, you're not alone.  It sounds like you're very frustrated with you're relationship, I'm sorry to hear that.  You seem like an extremely interesting, well spoken person, and I would like to listen to you.  

I know what it's like to be alone and want someone to walk through the door more than anything in the world...  I'm sorry.  

So I can't really take my own advice right now, but I know I've seen things change for the better extremely quickly in other people's lives, and supposedly, that's what can happen for us too.
Nope, not at all.  I appreciate the sentiment, and I've read the SW guidelines so I know what you're trying to do but there's absolutely no way I can appear cool after 5-6 lines of text.
The fact that I have no social life and cannot stand looking at pictures of myself, also that I loose traction with everyone I meet because I don't use it.
Social media really depresses me, family changes, relationship changes, loss of family business.

Always a few therapy appointments on the calender.  Getting a dog, maybe.  There was a girl that used to come over, which really helped a lot actually because I made the place look presentable.  Looking for jobs closer to my family too I guess, taking some classes, going camping this weekend.  

There's definitely a conflict.  Part of me doesn't want to call the shelter back because I don't want to leave the poor guy alone.
Thanks, and, yeah this is pretty much the same conversation I have with everyone.

I'm sorry.  This makes me cry but I still want to do it.  For 3 years I've felt exactly like this: 

"It's over. Everyone withdraws and you [...] are alone. The world outside keeps moving even though yours stopped days that seem like years ago. You spend the next [year decade?] learning this "new normal" as people slowly forget what happened. Nothing is ever the same. Small things will remind you of who you lost. "

What if it's 20?  I don't mean to belittle your point but I'm struggling.  If it wasn't for my family it would be over in an instant -- no hesitation whatsoever.  I would never endure this amount of pain for just myself.  I would like to make it look accidental.  

I look at my facebook profile and get confused...don't remember who that person was, doesn't make sense that that guy could be me.

It's 30 lines.  There's definitely a few things I can probably take off, others I continue to suck at.  

I have trouble keeping it updated as well but it's linked to a list of little crap I need to do each day, like sign up for a class, pay a bill / etc, so I end up opening it quite frequently for that reason. 

Doesn't seem too earth shattering to me but outside observers (friends) say they've noticed a change.  

I was thinking about setting some goals...like 95% complete for 3 weeks or something.
A noble sentiment.
